items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a Bayesian time-domain finite element (FE) model updating framework to mitigate parameter estimation bias induced by modeling error. In conventional Bayesian model updating, the discrepancy between measured and predicted responses, the prediction error, is typically modeled as zero-mean, stationary Gaussian white noise with prescribed covariance. This assumption, though adequate for accurate models, is often violated in practice by idealizations, simplifications, and unmodeled mechanisms, causing the prediction error to become structured and correlated in time and space, biasing parameter estimates. To address this, the proposed framework treats the prediction error&apos;s mean and covariance as unknown random quantities, estimated jointly with the FE parameters via a new Bayesian formulation, modeling the mean as normal and the covariance as inverse Wishart to infer time-varying, spatially correlated error statistics from response data. The framework is validated using simulated data from a nonlinear building structure under three modeling-error scenarios: geometric uncertainty, damping misrepresentation, and neglected nonstructural components. Results show the method reduces estimation bias, improves predictive accuracy, and produces more stable parameter estimates than a conventional parameter-only approach. Although performance may deteriorate when the prediction error departs substantially from the Gaussian assumption, the framework remains robust and significantly outperforms the conventional approach.</jats:p>
title: Mitigating Modeling Error Effects in Finite Element Model Updating: A Bayesian Framework for Joint Parameter–Prediction Error Estimation
